refuted_claims:
I recomputed everything from the 1,222 raw cells in /data/feasibility/E4/run-v2/cells, the v3 TRAINING cells and the LiveMath training pool, which I loaded through the frozen data.pool. My scripts and outputs are in /data/feasibility/E4-critic/ (critic_check.py/.json, v3_check.py, v3_gap.py, v3_second_send.py, sheet_officeqa.py). Local copies are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-dulin-Documents-Paper-SkillOpt/e7258b97-b430-4dd5-959d-eb871e7c777f/scratchpad/feas/E4-critic/. I made no paid calls and opened no test pools.

R1. Claim: "Generic QA-card gain ~+7 on every QA target" (verdict_cn: any QA card beats the empty scaffold by about 7 points on any QA target).
- What I checked: I split each target's column by the two artefacts the explorer had itself found.
- SearchQA: the whole gain sits on the 7 complete items where the scaffold gave an untagged reply. Without them (n=33) the five cards score 0.0, +1.5, +1.5, -4.5 and -3.0. Every CI contains 0 (up/down 2/2, 1/1, 3/2, 2/4, 1/3).
- LiveMath: 17 of the 41 complete items carry the meta option, and it is the key in 17/17. The scaffold picked it in 0 of 37 cells, the cards in 3 to 6 of 37. That stratum supplies most of each card's gain: 3.6 of 6.1 (SearchQA card), 6.1 of 7.3 (OfficeQA card, a "similar" cell), 3.6 of 8.5 (own card) and 7.3 of 12.2 (SpreadsheetBench card).
- LiveMath, the 24 non-meta items: +4.2, +2.1, +8.3, +8.3, -8.3. All unresolved.
- Mean of the 3 QA cards minus scaffold after removing these strata: SearchQA +1.0 [-3.0,+5.6]; OfficeQA +6.7 [-2.2,+16.1] (unchanged); LiveMath +4.9 [-3.5,+15.3].
- Caveat: the SearchQA cut conditions on the scaffold's outcome, so it is a decomposition, not an unbiased estimate. Still, the "+7" is format repair plus meta-option picks, not a demonstrated generic-instruction effect.
- Prior work not cited: on 10/12-10/13 this project already measured a 3-line generic instruction at +9.6 and BCB coding texts at +6-7 over empty, on 250 SearchQA items.

R2. Claim: "Identical requests sent within 1 s return reformatted, untagged answers ... 0 flips in the 23 pairs sent at least 120 s apart" (verdict_cn: with two minutes or more between requests not one item flipped; a fixable defect).
- What I checked: flips by send gap for every arm.
- The 0/23 holds only for the SearchQA scaffold.
- SearchQA card arms flip MORE when lagged: 11/106 (10.4%) vs 6/94 (6.4%) back-to-back. LiveMath cards: 9/111 vs 11/94. LiveMath scaffold: 2/22 vs 2/19.
- All arms pooled: SearchQA 11/129 vs 11/111; LiveMath 11/133 vs 13/113.
- 2 of the 7 untagged SearchQA scaffold replies came 120 s or more after their twin.
- v3 has the same scaffold text on the same items (E-ds s1). Its 8 twin pairs sent less than 2 s apart had 0 flips; its 138 pairs sent 120 s or more apart had 5. Untagged replies there split evenly: 2 on first sends, 2 on second sends.
- In E4 the send gap is fully confounded with the launch period, because the lag was introduced mid-run at 00:51.
- So this is a one-arm, one-benchmark association. Spacing sends is harmless, but it does not lower the 8-10% flip floor.

R3. Claim: "Cell replication ... Pearson -0.50; mean |run0-run1| = 9.3 points".
- What I checked: the same correlation per target, on the same items.
- It is a Simpson effect. Between runs the scaffold fell 12.5 points on SearchQA (65.0 to 52.5) and rose 9.8 on LiveMath (26.8 to 36.6), which pushed each target's five cells in opposite directions.
- Within LiveMath, r = +0.73. Within SearchQA, r = -0.17, but that says little: the run-1 cells only span 10.0-12.5.
- After removing the shared scaffold shift, the mean run-to-run difference falls from 9.0 to 3.8 points (SearchQA) and from 9.7 to 3.9 (LiveMath).

R4. Claim: "Retire the registered similarity map". verdict_cn also turns H1's +0.1 [-5.6,+5.5] into "no difference", which treats absence of evidence as evidence of absence.
- What gets transferred: whole task cards. The rendered Skills are 2.4-3.5 KB and mostly answer-contract directives, not learned rules of at most 600 characters.
- Placement: the dissimilar cells use placements the protocol never makes, e.g. ALFWorld <action> bullets under the OfficeQA heading. In the real evolve-on-one design, text stays under its own heading, where cal-1 measured +0.2 [-3.1,+3.6] (SearchQA only).
- H1 is decided by two OfficeQA channel cells that cancel: -20.0 in the similar group, -26.7 in the dissimilar group.
- Resolution is about 5.5 points, while learned-rule effects are +1-3 points.
- So H1 cannot speak to whether learned rules transfer along the registered pairs.
- Literature: Vu et al., EMNLP 2020 (arXiv 2005.00770) find that task/domain similarity does matter, along with data size and complexity. Su et al., NAACL 2022 (arXiv 2111.06719) find that measured indicators predict prompt transfer best. That supports measuring similarity, not discarding the map.

R5. Claim: the SpreadsheetBench card costs OfficeQA 20 points because it demands Python.
- What I checked: all 7 OfficeQA items it lost.
- Only 2 of 7 (UID0228, UID0239) contain Python, and it sits inside the answer tag. 2 of 7 (UID0070, UID0133) put the whole reasoning inside the tag. 3 of 7 (UID0044, UID0072, UID0115) are bare answers with no reasoning, at most 10 completion tokens.
- The explorer's own decomposition labels all 7 "clean" (0 channel breaks).
- The SpreadsheetBench and ALFWorld cards share one mechanism: answer-only replies. Median reply length is 18-29 characters on SearchQA and LiveMath.
- "Almost no effect on SearchQA and math" also hides that the ALFWorld card broke the answer tag in 24 of 85 LiveMath cells, all of which failed; meta-option picks offset that loss.

R6. Claim: OfficeQA (74) and ALFWorld (57) can only show effects of about 9 points or more, however much is spent.
- 74 and 57 are the pinned TRAINING pools.
- Under "evolve on one, evaluate on the rest", nothing is learned on the evaluation benchmarks, so their whole item sets are usable.
- OfficeQA-Full has 246 questions (133 Pro plus 113 easier; arXiv 2603.08655). That gives about ±4.8 points at the measured SD of 0.385.
- ALFWorld has 3,553 training games and 274 evaluation games. It is limited by cost, not by items.
- More runs per item also shrink the run-noise part of the SD.
- The SD used is from card-vs-empty comparisons, not from rule-vs-good-instruction comparisons.

R7. Claim: cross-day comparisons are unreliable.
- The drift is specific to the scaffold: -5.9 [-9.9,-1.9] (n=200).
- The five-card Skill moved only -0.5 [-2.8,+1.6] (n=199).

R8. The LiveMath meta-option "side finding" is already in D7's report (docs/handoff/feasibility-20261021/D7/report.md, 129/129). Recommendation 4, which offers LiveMath as an evolution benchmark, conflicts with this artefact.

R9. Two smaller points.
- The LiveMath run-0 positives (O +13.6, Sh +18.2) are measured against the scaffold's weaker run (26.8%) and are driven by the meta option.
- "A few minutes apart" is inaccurate: about 40% of the twin pairs were sent 0 s apart.
confirmed_claims:
I checked the following against the raw data, and they hold.

Matrix and contrasts
- All 15 matrix cells reproduce exactly from the cells. Examples: ALFWorld card on OfficeQA -26.7 [-43.3,-13.3], 0 up/9 down, p=.0039; SpreadsheetBench card on OfficeQA -20.0, 0/7, p=.016; SpreadsheetBench card on LiveMath +12.2, 9/2; SearchQA card on OfficeQA +13.3, 5/1.
- Complete items: 40, 30 and 41. No cell passes the 15-cell Bonferroni threshold (the smallest p is .0039 against .0033).
- H1 arithmetic: similar 1.22 vs dissimilar 1.13, so +0.1.
- H2: +11.6, coming entirely from OfficeQA (+30.0 on OfficeQA alone; +1.7 [-3.5,+7.5] without it).
- The ALFWorld card's harm on OfficeQA is a real channel break: 7 of its 9 losses have an action tag or no answer tag.

Run accounting
- 1,222 of 1,650 cells were scored and 428 were stopped by the cap; 0 unknown.
- Truncations: 14, of which 13 on OfficeQA.
- Tokens: 3,558,474 in the run plus 117,695 in the smoke = 3,676,169. The cap bound at 02:07:21 (status.json).
- analysis_plan.json predates the launch (23:57). Post-hoc analyses are labelled. The identity checks are true.
- data.pool returns the registered TRAINING pool (historical train + val parts), not a test pool. Pool sizes: 600, 74, 283, 120, 57.

Noise
- Discordant item-pairs: 22/240 (SearchQA) and 24/246 (LiveMath).
- The scaffold moved -12.5 and +9.8 points between its two runs.
- The scaffold drifted -5.9 across sessions; the cal-1 same-text null was +0.3 [-1.8,+2.3].
- About 10% flips at temperature 0 is typical in the literature: Atil et al., arXiv 2408.04667, report accuracy swings of up to 15% across runs.

v3 comparison
- Recomputed from the v3 s1 TRAINING cells: I-ds minus E-ds on SearchQA = +3.25 [-0.25,+6.75], 20 up/11 down, n=200. The explorer's figure is right.
- The shared context.md "preview" (+0.089, 36 up/12 down) does NOT match these cells. The main session should re-check it.

Power and costs
- Arithmetic correct: 115/228/146 items for a 5-point half-width and 318/634/404 for 3 points.
- The ~15M-token estimate for the QA matrix (4,690 cells) and ~29M for ALFWorld are consistent with the measured tokens per cell.

LiveMath meta option
- In the 283 training items it appears 129 times and is the key 129/129 (68/155 in the train part, 61/128 in the val part).
- Its letter is spread across positions: A 23, B 24, C 28, D 20, E 34. This matches D7.

Supporting literature
- Large format effects are expected: Sclar et al., ICLR 2024, report gaps of up to 76 points from formatting alone.
- Recommendation 2 is sound: use a strong instruction in the same session, interleaved, as the reference, never the empty scaffold. It matches the owner's good-instruction yardstick and the 10/13 project lesson.
missing:
1) Stratified reads. The LiveMath column should be read split by meta and non-meta items, and the SearchQA column with and without the scaffold's format failures; the headline structure changes once this is done (see R1).

2) A realistic placement arm. Each card should also be measured under its own heading on OfficeQA and LiveMath, which is what an evolve-on-one Skill actually looks like there. Format-stripped cards would separate content from channel, and a generic-instruction arm is needed in the pilot itself, not only in the proposed full study.

3) The right objects to transfer. The owner's question is whether LEARNED text transfers, so the transferred texts should be learned rules: the 49 v3 proposals, or the cal-1 seed-rule, seed-rule3 and cand texts. Task cards are not learned rules.

4) The structural design question. With one section per benchmark and an "Applies when" line, a Skill evolved on one benchmark has nothing in the other sections. v5 must choose either a shared general section or copy-placement. These data imply that copied text must be format-neutral, i.e. it must not carry answer-channel or length directives.

5) The link to purpose 1, which the pilot never addresses. The verifier rubric could:
- encode each target's answer contract and reject a transferred rule whose directives conflict with it;
- audit construction regularities before evolution, such as the meta option, so the Skill does not learn shortcuts that cannot transfer;
- feed similar-target generated panels (D6/D12).

6) Correct evaluation-pool sizing. Pool the evaluation benchmarks' full item sets, e.g. OfficeQA-Full with 246 questions and ALFWorld's public 3,553 + 274 games. Then compute power for a rule-vs-good-instruction comparison (an effect of 1-3 points) at 80% power. For example, an SD of 0.25 and an effect of 3 points need about 540 items, which OfficeQA cannot supply.

7) Prior project evidence. The 10/13 cross-bench selection and foreign-text studies are not cited: SearchQA to BCB showed no transfer, and BCB to SearchQA gave +6-7, below a 3-line generic instruction.

8) Untested cells. The registered OfficeQA<->SpreadsheetBench pair and both heavy targets are unmeasured. The "no drop on dissimilar" part of the owner's yardstick is never tested in the realistic own-section configuration.
notes_cn:
【E4 复核结论：部分成立】
E4 是什么：把五个题库各自的"做题说明卡"（人写的做题说明）交叉放到别的题库上，看"相似的题库"到底指什么。

一、核对过、属实的部分
- 原始数据没问题。我用 1,222 条原始记录把 15 个格子全部重算了一遍，数字完全一致。
- 花费 367.6 万 token（模型读写文字的计量单位），在 02:07 因预算上限停下，只用了训练题。这些都属实。分析计划确实在开跑前就写好了。
- 数学题库（LiveMath）里有一个特殊选项，内容是"其余某个选项正确，但能证明更强的结论"。283 道训练题里有 129 道带它，这 129 道的正确答案全是它。属实，但 D7 方向早就发现了，不是新发现。
- 同一段说明、同一批题再做一遍，约十分之一的题会对错翻转。属实，也符合公开文献：有论文测到，即使把随机性调到最低，多次运行的准确率也能相差 15%。

二、站不住的结论
1. "任何一张问答说明卡都比空白模板高约 7 分"（空白模板＝只有五个题库标题、不含任何做题说明的版本）。拆开看，几乎全是两个假象：
   - 搜索问答：增益全部来自 7 道"空白模板没写答案标签"的题。去掉这 7 道后剩 33 道，五张卡的差别都在 −4.5 到 +1.5 分之间，等于没有。
   - 数学题：41 道里有 17 道带那个特殊选项，它永远是正确答案。空白模板一次都没选它，说明卡偶尔会选。每张卡的"提升"里，有 42% 到 84% 就来自这里。去掉这 17 道，剩下 24 道题上没有一张卡的效果能确定。
2. "两次请求隔开 2 分钟以上就不再翻转，这是个可修的毛病"。只在"搜索问答＋空白模板"这一个组合里成立（23 对里 0 次翻转）。
   - 带说明卡的组合，隔开发送后翻转反而更多（10.4% 对 6.4%）。数学题上隔开了也照样翻转。
   - 旧的 v3 实验里，同一段空白模板紧挨着发了 8 对，一次也没翻转。
   - "隔开发送"是跑到一半才改的，和时间段完全重合，分不清是哪个原因。
   - 所以隔开发送可以做，没有坏处，但降不了约 10% 的噪声。
3. "同一格子两遍算出的提升对不上（相关系数 −0.5）"。这是把两个题库混在一起算造成的假象。
   - 空白模板第二遍在搜索问答上掉了 12.5 分，在数学题上涨了 9.8 分，把两边的格子往相反方向推。
   - 单看数学题，两遍的相关系数是 +0.73，是对得上的。
   - 扣掉空白模板自己的晃动，两遍平均只差约 4 分。
4. "表格卡要求写 Python 程序，所以在文档问答上扣 20 分"。7 道丢分题里：
   - 只有 2 道真写了 Python；
   - 2 道把整段推理塞进了答案标签；
   - 3 道没推理，直接给一个数（只输出约 10 个 token）。
   更准确的说法是"这张卡让模型不推理了"，而文档问答需要计算。
5. "事先登记的相似题库对没用，应该废掉"。证据不够，原因有四：
   - 这次搬过去的是整张说明卡，内容主要是"答案怎么写"的格式要求，不是学出来的规则。
   - 很多"不相似"格子是把家务卡硬塞到文档问答的标题下，真实流程里根本不会这样放。
   - 两组的结果主要被文档问答上的两个大伤害左右，而这两个伤害正好一组一个，互相抵消了。
   - 这个检验只能分辨 5 分以上的差别，而学到的规则通常只有 1–3 分的效果。
   所以它说明不了"学到的规则会不会沿着相似对迁移"。
6. "文档问答、家务题无论花多少钱都只能看出 9 分以上的差别"。前提错了：74 和 57 只是训练题的数量。
   - "在一个题库进化、在其余题库评测"时，评测题库的所有题都能用。
   - 文档问答公开全集有 246 题，误差约 ±4.8 分。
   - 家务题公开的有 3,553 个训练游戏加 274 个评测游戏，只是贵，不是没题。
7. "跨天比较不可靠"。不稳的其实是空白模板，换一天掉了 5.9 分。五张说明卡组成的版本换一天只差 0.5 分（199 道题）。

三、对你两个目标的意义
- 目标 2（在一个题库进化、其余题库评测），真正站得住的有三条：
  (1) 对照组要用好的说明卡，同一时段、交错着测，不能用空白模板（项目 10/13 已有同样的教训）。
  (2) 带"答案格式"要求的文字搬到别的题库会伤人，想要迁移的规则必须和格式要求分开写。
  (3) 数学题库那个特殊选项会让"任何改动"看起来都有效果，评测时要把这类题单独算。不建议用数学题库当进化用的题库。
- 目标 1（Skill 和验证端的评分规则一起进化）：这次完全没涉及。可以补两件事：
  - 让验证端记下每个题库的答案格式，装规则前自动检查有没有格式冲突；
  - 先查出题库本身的"答案规律"（比如那个特殊选项），免得 Skill 学到不能迁移的捷径。

四、可行性：低
- 跑起来不难：全套问答矩阵约 1,500 万 token。
- 但按现在的设计，主要测到的是上面这些假象。
- 就算重新设计，也只能看出 5 分以上的差别，比学到的规则的效果大得多。
